clue.text: Not properly two-dimensional, thus enough for 13 6

definitions.note: 13 and 6 are the answers EDWARD LEAR and POEM, so the definition is a poem by Lear

indicators.note: not properly set out, so the letters of the three fodder words are jumbled into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone complains that a drawing is not quite flat, but decides it will do for a poem.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not properly' rearranges all 24 letters of TWO-DIMENSIONAL plus THUS ENOUGH; 'for' links. 13 and 6 are EDWARD LEAR and POEM.
explanation.definitionFit: The Dong with a Luminous Nose is a nonsense ballad written by Edward Lear in 1876.

clue.text: Team sent north in Hirosaki or Tokyo

indicators.note: sent north says the hidden letters are read backwards
in says the answer sits concealed within the words that follow it

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A sports team is posted north to play in two Japanese cities.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft's parse stands; only 'in' is named as the signal for the concealed run. In a down answer 'sent north' turns AKIORT upward.
explanation.definitionFit: A troika is a Russian carriage drawn by a team of three horses, hence any group of three.

clue.text: Despite that 50/50 bet, nothing!

parts.note: a bet with equal chances is placed at evens, odds of 1 to 1
nothing is zero, the letter O

explanation.surface: A gambler laments that despite a coin-toss wager, the payout was zero.
explanation.definitionFit: Even so is an adverbial phrase meaning nevertheless, conceding a point while carrying on.

clue.text: Potatoes mashed to go with healthy skin treatment?

indicators.note: mashed potatoes are crushed into a new form, so the word is rearranged
the skin of the word is its outside, so its first and last letters are kept

explanation.surface: A health tip: eat mashed potatoes for good skin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'skin' looks like part of a skincare treatment but picks the outer letters H and Y of 'healthy'. The question mark admits that osteopathy is one example of a treatment.
explanation.definitionFit: Osteopathy is a therapy manipulating bones and muscles, so it is one kind of medical treatment.

clue.text: Deep rough sound from Greek hunting bird

parts.note: an owl is a bird of prey that hunts at night

explanation.surface: A Greek bird of prey gives a low harsh cry.
explanation.definitionFit: A growl is the low guttural noise a dog or angry person makes.

clue.text: Dead end that is restricting motorway flow

indicators.note: restricting means hemming in, so the first piece encloses the others

parts.note: i.e. abbreviates id est, Latin for that is
M is the abbreviation for motorway, as in the M1
to pass is to move or flow along, as time passes

explanation.surface: A traffic report: a dead end is choking the flow of motorway traffic.
explanation.definitionFit: An impasse is a deadlock or blind alley from which there is no way forward.

clue.text: By that cheapest possible settee, cot collapses

parts.note: 1p, one penny, is the smallest British price, read as the letters IP
a settee is a sofa

indicators.note: a collapsing cot falls into a different shape, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A bargain-basement settee ends with a cot falling apart in a cheap furniture shop.
explanation.walkthrough: The trick is 1p, one penny, the cheapest possible British price, written as IP. 'collapses' turns COT into CTO.
explanation.definitionFit: Ipso facto is Latin for by the fact itself, used to mean by that very fact.

clue.text: Johnson's written about Old English verse

indicators.note: written about here means placed around, so the first piece goes round the second

parts.note: Boris Johnson was Prime Minister, PM, when the puzzle appeared; the 's is a contracted is

explanation.surface: Samuel Johnson has written about Old English verse.
explanation.walkthrough: Johnson looks like the lexicographer Samuel Johnson, but is Boris Johnson, the Prime Minister (PM) at the time.
explanation.definitionFit: A poem is a piece of verse; the singular noun stands for a single composition.

clue.text: University burning outside former capital

indicators.note: outside says the first piece wraps around the second

parts.note: a burning wound is sore
Bonn was the capital of West Germany before reunification

explanation.surface: A university is ablaze on the edge of an old capital city.
explanation.definitionFit: The Sorbonne is the historic university in Paris.

clue.text: Perhaps Midwest ground that's avoided?

parts.note: read as mid-west, the middle letters of the word west; perhaps flags this odd reading
ground is the past tense of grind, as teeth grind food, so chewed

explanation.surface: A question about whether American heartland soil is shunned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Midwest' looks like the US region but is split as mid-west: the middle of WEST is ES. 'ground' is the past of grind, not soil.
explanation.definitionFit: To eschew something is to deliberately keep away from it, so eschewed is shunned.

clue.text: Public upset when vase goes missing

indicators.note: goes missing says the named piece is taken away

parts.note: to upset something is to overturn it
an urn is a vase

explanation.surface: Someone is publicly upset because a vase has disappeared.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' is not an anagram signal here but a synonym: OVERTURN, which loses its URN.
explanation.definitionFit: Overt means done openly, not hidden, so public in the sense of plainly visible.

clue.text: Dealing with Labour, bitter, so involved with Conservative

indicators.note: involved means tangled up, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Political talk: the Labour Party, bitter, gets entangled with the Conservatives.
explanation.walkthrough: Labour looks like the British political party; it is childbirth.
explanation.definitionFit: Obstetric describes the branch of medicine concerned with childbirth, when a mother is in labour.

clue.text: Repeated blows bringing one round?

parts.note: sounds like a boxer revived after a beating, but describes breathing air into the lungs of someone unconscious

explanation.walkthrough: Blows suggests punches; here they are breaths blown into a casualty's mouth, and bringing round means reviving.
explanation.definitionFit: Mouth-to-mouth resuscitation involves rhythmically blowing air into a casualty's lungs to revive them.

clue.text: See 1
Author of 2 Kings

definitions.meaning: a writer, here the Victorian nonsense poet
two kings: Edward, as in several English monarchs, and Shakespeare's King Lear

explanation.walkthrough: 2 Kings looks like the book of the Bible; it means simply two kings, named one after the other.
explanation.definitionFit: Edward Lear was a Victorian writer famous for limericks and nonsense verse.

clue.text: Coming into hectic canteen, surrender priority

indicators.note: coming into means entering, so one piece goes inside the other
a hectic scene is chaotic, so the letters are thrown into disorder

parts.note: to cede is to give up or surrender

explanation.surface: Someone arrives in a busy works canteen and gives up their place in the queue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hectic' scrambles the fodder to ANTENCE, and 'Coming into' splits that after its fourth letter to take in the synonym for surrender.
explanation.definitionFit: Antecedence is the state of coming before, which is precedence or priority.

clue.text: Bear moving in woods pauses for refreshment

indicators.note: in says one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: teak is a hardwood, so teaks are woods

indicators.note: moving here means shifting about, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A bear wandering through the forest stops for a snack.
explanation.walkthrough: 'moving' scrambles the animal to BREA, which goes 'in' the woods after their third letter. 'Bear' looks like the subject of the sentence but is only fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Tea breaks are short rests from work taken for a hot drink.

clue.text: Plant key seen beneath reptile house

indicators.note: in a down answer beneath means after, so this piece follows the others

parts.note: an asp is a venomous snake
Del is the delete key on a computer keyboard

explanation.surface: A plant has been spotted under the reptile house at the zoo.
explanation.walkthrough: Key is not a musical key but the Del key on a keyboard.
explanation.definitionFit: The asphodel is a lily-family flower, in legend covering the meadows of the Greek underworld.

clue.text: See 1
State facts about defeat on last point in tennis?

parts.note: the last letter of tennis is S, the compass point South, taken in full

indicators.note: about means around, so the first piece encloses the second

parts.note: facts are data
KO, knockout, is a defeat in boxing

explanation.surface: A sports report recounts how a tennis match was lost on the final point.
explanation.walkthrough: 'last point in tennis' is the letter S, the compass point it abbreviates read in full; 'on' puts DAKOTA after it.
explanation.definitionFit: South Dakota is a US state in the Midwest.

clue.text: Weapon an American lawyer ships

parts.note: an arm is a weapon, as in firearms
an gives the article A
a DA is a district attorney, a US prosecutor

explanation.surface: An American lawyer is shipping a weapon.
explanation.definitionFit: An armada is a large fleet of warships, most famously the Spanish one of 1588.

clue.text: Legend of Tees? It's rubbish

parts.note: Tees is the setter, so something belonging to Tees is the setter's, my
read as leg end, the foot is the end of the leg

explanation.surface: Someone dismisses a tale about the River Tees as nonsense.
explanation.walkthrough: Tees is this puzzle's setter, so 'of Tees' gives MY; 'Legend' splits as leg end.
explanation.definitionFit: My foot! is an exclamation of disbelief meaning that what was said is nonsense.

clue.text: Salute an icy aerial bombardment?

definitions.meaning: ice pellets falling from the sky, likened to an attack from the air

explanation.definitionFit: Hail means both a greeting and pellets of ice that fall like a barrage from the clouds.

clue.text: Top horse race in China

parts.note: the crown is the top of something, such as a head or hill
the Derby is a famous English flat horse race at Epsom

explanation.surface: A leading racehorse competes in China.
explanation.walkthrough: China looks like the country; it is porcelain.
explanation.definitionFit: Crown Derby is a fine porcelain made in Derby, England, so a kind of china tableware.

clue.text: See 1
Daughter regularly taking ecstasy is finished

parts.note: someone on a drug or medicine takes it regularly
E is slang for an ecstasy tablet

explanation.surface: A worried parent says a daughter who uses ecstasy habitually is ruined.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' is not picking alternate letters; 'regularly taking' means on (drugs).
explanation.definitionFit: Done means completed or over, as in the job is done.

clue.text: Mum's one old bird without energy to join rave

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the first piece goes around the second

parts.note: the dodo is an extinct bird
E is the symbol for energy in physics
to rave is to rant

explanation.surface: A mother's ancient bird, lacking energy, takes up raving.
explanation.walkthrough: Mum is a British brand of deodorant, so 'Mum's one' means an example of what Mum is.
explanation.definitionFit: Mum is a long-established British brand of antiperspirant, so a deodorant is what it is.

clue.text: I'm grateful to retire in bedroom regularly finding muse

indicators.note: in says one piece goes inside the other
taking letters at regular intervals, here the second, fourth and sixth
to retire is to go back, so the word for thanks is turned round

parts.note: ta is British informal for thank you

explanation.surface: Someone thanks their partner as they go to bed, and finds inspiration there.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' takes ERO from bEdRoOm; 'to retire' turns TA into AT, placed 'in' it.
explanation.definitionFit: Erato is the Greek Muse of lyric and love poetry.

clue.text: Not as much freedom from anxiety reported for tenants

indicators.note: reported means spoken, so the result is a word that sounds the same

parts.words: Not as much freedom from anxiety
parts.note: less means not as much; ease is freedom from worry

explanation.surface: Renters report getting less peace of mind.
explanation.walkthrough: LESS plus EASE, said aloud, sounds like the plural noun.
explanation.definitionFit: Lessees are people who hold a lease, the renters of a property.

clue.text: American brute keeping right up to date

indicators.note: keeping means holding inside, so one piece contains the other

parts.note: a brute is a beast

explanation.surface: An American thug stays right on the latest news.
explanation.definitionFit: To keep abreast of events is an idiom for staying informed and current.
